snippet.title: Deu o que Falar: Relembre o caso da menina de 12 anos morta após sair para patinar
snippet.description:
Em junho de 2018, a tranquila cidade de Araçariguama (SP), com cerca de 28 mil habitantes, foi abalada pelo desaparecimento de Vitória Gabrielly. A jovem de 12 anos saiu para patinar e não voltou mais. Dias depois, seu corpo foi encontrado em uma área rural, em um crime que chocou o Brasil pela brutalidade.

Vitória foi abordada por criminosos enquanto voltava para casa e forçada a entrar em um carro. Amigos e familiares mobilizaram-se rapidamente, e a polícia iniciou uma busca intensa, considerando o caso como potencial sequestro desde o início.

Investigadores infiltraram-se em comunidades locais e cães farejadores foram utilizados. Uma virada crucial ocorreu quando Júlio Ergesse confessou sua participação, revelando ter agido junto com Bruno Oliveira e Mayara Borges sob ordens de Odilan Alves Sobrinho. Eles a confundiram com outra menina, alvo de uma cobrança de dívida do tráfico.

Após prisões e coleta de provas, incluindo genéticas, todos foram condenados: Júlio a mais de duas décadas, Bruno e Mayara a penas mais longas, e Odilan como mandante.

snippet.title: Karl Bushby completes 28-year journey from Chile to Hull | BBC News
snippet.description:
British adventurer Karl Bushby has completed his 31,000-mile (50,000 km) journey from South America to Hull in the UK, reuniting with his mother at the family home 28 years after setting off.
 
In November 1998, the former paratrooper, then aged 29, set off from Punta Arenas, Chile, to complete an unbroken path back home, without breaking two self-imposed rules: not to return to the UK until the end of the journey, and not to use transport to advance.
 
Bushby said only about 15 of the 28 years were spent walking, with struggles obtaining visas, the 2007 global economic crash and Covid blamed for delays.

He often retreated to Mexico, where costs are low, between stints.

Under the rules he set for his journey, Bushby could not return to the UK to meet his family.

But Lakshmi, a Class 10 student from the Zilla Parishad High School in Raptadu, Anantapur district, has won the hearts of millions with her extraordinary courage. When a merciless attacker wielding an electric saw went on a violent rampage, she risked her own life to protect her classmate. Even though she knew that confronting him could cost her life, she bravely stood up to him and fought back. The incident took place on Saturday morning, October 31, at Raptadu Zilla Parishad High School. A mathematics class was underway under the supervision of teacher Rajeshwari. He suddenly attacked Gopika, who was sitting in the front row, with an electric saw. While the other students ran away in fear, Lakshmi refused to back down. Without worrying about her own safety, she stood in front of the attacker and tried to protect her classmate. During the struggle, Lakshmi suffered serious injuries to her leg. Her courage and willingness to risk her own life to save Gopika moved the entire nation. Immediately after the attack, both girls were rushed to a hospital in Anantapur. Following the Chief Minister's instructions, critically injured Gopika was shifted to Manipal Hospital in Bengaluru through a special Green Corridor, where she underwent surgeries. Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu also appreciated Lakshmi's courage. Meanwhile, 15 special police teams were formed to track down Hemanth, who had fled after the attack. On November 1, he was located in the Atmakur forest area near Dharmavaram. When he allegedly attacked the police with stones and a knife, the police opened fire in self-defence. Hemanth sustained serious injuries and was admitted to a hospital. Lakshmi! Your bravery and courage are an inspiration to society. We sincerely pray for your speedy recovery. snippet.title: Prada Just Went Anti-AI and Drew Its Holiday Campaign By Hand
snippet.description:
Prada's Holiday 2026 campaign is literally called Drawing Prada, and its animation was drawn by hand under John Pomeroy, an animator who started at Disney in 1973 and worked on Winnie the Pooh and Pocahontas. It lands after Coca-Cola made its last two Christmas ads with AI and McDonald's Netherlands pulled its AI holiday ad three days after posting it. Prada calls the campaign "a celebration of craft and process," made with "old-school techniques from the golden era of cartoons," and released a behind-the-scenes video to prove people drew every frame. The video also traces the word cartoon back to the full-scale designs Raphael and his workshop painted around 1515 for the Sistine Chapel tapestries, now at the V&A in London, and to the 1843 Punch joke that gave the word its modern meaning.
